basis: Umbrella of transplant-related immune and immunosuppression disorders; no single damaged organ is common across the group.
Inherited iron overload with predominant hepatic deposition; iron-related arthropathy affects ~30–50% of clinically affected patients; cardiac injury is less common.
Axonal neuropathy with defining vocal cord paresis; contractures and neuropathic spinal arthropathy each occur in 3/9 patients (~33%).
Neoplasm occupying the brainstem.
Major congenital cardiac malformations; asplenia in 4/14 (~29%) is near the 30% threshold. Visceral positional changes alone do not establish organ damage.
KCNA2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures, developmental impairment and ataxia are neurologic.
Periosteal bone thickening and pachydermia define the disorder; both occur in 2/2 annotated patients. Diarrhea alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Spastic paraplegia with defining kyphoscoliosis and neuromyopathy; limb and tongue atrophy are frequent (30–79%).
Hair, sweat-gland and skin abnormalities define this ectodermal dysplasia; inflammatory blepharitis occurs in 2/2 annotated patients.
Tick-borne infectious illness; the transient erythema migrans-like rash does not establish lasting skin damage.
Definition specifies inherited predisposition to myeloid blood/marrow neoplasms; this does not imply an existing neoplasm or damage to other organs.
Bacterial infection of the neonatal urinary tract.
Occlusion of a major cerebral supplying artery causes ischemic brain injury.
Compensatory overexpansion of lung tissue; confined to the pulmonary axis.
DSC2-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy; definition specifies isolated cardiac disease. Skin and hair findings are not established as common.
Motor neuron disease; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 80–99%. Partial androgen insensitivity commonly causes endocrine dysfunction, with related signs in 80–99%.
Malignant transformation of an eccrine spiradenoma indicates sweat-gland/adnexal origin in the breast region, supporting the skin axis.
Congenital cardiac and great-vessel malformations define the disease; anxiety and depression have no organ axis.
Isolated hereditary high-frequency hearing loss.
Defined by pneumoconiosis with rheumatoid pulmonary nodules and autoimmune rheumatoid arthritis.
Visceral bacterial infection predominantly affects the lungs; liver, spleen, kidney and brain involvement is not established in ≥30%.
Congenital extraocular motility impairment and ptosis; extraocular muscles belong to the ocular apparatus.
Ocular accommodative strain or muscle imbalance; associated headache does not establish neurologic injury.
Spinocerebellar degeneration and defining loss of pupillary function; limited phenotype detail supports no additional axes.
Choline deficiency impairs hepatic lipid export; fatty liver/injury occurs in roughly half or more in human depletion studies. Supplied definition chiefly describes animals.
